etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French confiner, from confins, from Medieval Latin confines, from Latin confinium, from confīnis.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) To have a common boundary with; to border on. [16th–19th c.]

quote.citation: 1667, John Milton, “Book II”, in Paradise Lost. […], London:  […]  [Samuel Simmons], and are to be sold by Peter Parker […]; [a]nd by Robert Boulter […]; [a]nd Matthias Walker, […], →OCLC; republished as Paradise Lost in Ten Books: […], London: Basil Montagu Pickering […], 1873, →OCLC:
quote.text: Where your gloomy bounds / Confine with heaven

quote.citation: 1717, John Dryden, “Book XII”, in Ovid’s Metamorphoses in Fifteen Books. […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Betwixt heaven and earth and skies there stands a place / Confining on all three.

quote.citation: 1791, James Boswell, Life of Johnson, Oxford, published 2008, page 467:
quote.text: ‘Why, Sir, to be sure, such parts of Sclavonia as confine with Germany, will borrow German words; and such parts as confine with Tartary will borrow Tartar words.’

definitions.definition: (transitive) To restrict (someone or something) to a particular scope or area; to keep in or within certain bounds. [from 17th c.]

quote.citation: c. 1596–1599 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Second Part of Henry the Fourth, […]”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene i]:
quote.text: Now let not nature's hand / Keep the wild flood confined! let order die!

quote.citation: 1680, John Dryden, Ovid’s Epistles translated by several hands, London: Jacob Tonson, Preface,[1]
quote.text: He is to confine himself to the compass of numbers and the slavery of rhyme.

definitions.definition: (chiefly in the plural) A boundary or limit.

quote.citation: a. 1917, anonymous, “Lord Bateman” (folk song) as published in Bertrand Harris Bronson (1959) The Traditional Tunes of the Child Ballads, vol. 1, p. 419:
quote.text: She says for you to bring her a slice of cake,A bottle of the best wine,And not to forget the fair young ladyThat did release you from close confine.
